key_insight: PEFT-Arena reframes evaluation of parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT) as a stability–plasticity problem, showing that methods that excel at task adaptation often sacrifice pretrained capabilities. A joint benchmark measuring both downstream accuracy and capability retention reveals distinct stability–plasticity trade-offs across PEFT methods.
problem_solved: Current PEFT evaluations focus almost exclusively on downstream accuracy and ignore how much of a model's pretrained abilities are forgotten after finetuning; PEFT-Arena provides a unified way to quantify both adaptation (plasticity) and retention (stability).
method: Design a benchmark suite that jointly measures downstream task performance and preservation of pretrained capabilities (language understanding, reasoning, robustness, etc.).
Define stability and plasticity metrics and map PEFT methods (e.g., LoRA, adapters, prompt tuning, BitFit) into a 2D stability–plasticity space across model sizes and parameter budgets.
Perform systematic experiments and analyses to identify factors (parameter budget, update pattern, rank, layer selection) that govern the stability–plasticity trade-off.
impact: Provides practitioners a principled way to choose and tune PEFT methods based on the desired balance between adapting to new tasks and retaining general capabilities, improving reliability, safety, and long-term usefulness of adapted LLMs. It also guides future PEFT design toward methods that better manage forgetting.
visual_elements: 2D stability–plasticity scatter plot that positions PEFT methods by downstream gain (plasticity) vs retained capability (stability).
Paired bar charts showing downstream accuracy vs pretrained-capability scores for each method to highlight trade-offs.
Heatmap of trade-offs across model sizes and parameter budgets to show how stability–plasticity regimes shift.
Pipeline diagram of PEFT-Arena: dataset groupings, metric computation (stability/plasticity), and evaluation workflow.
paper_title: PEFT-Arena: Understanding Parameter-Efficient Finetuning from a Stability-Plasticity Perspective
paper_authors: Yangyi Huang, Ruotian Peng, Zeju Qiu, Jiale Kang, Yandong Wen
